title: Google built an AI translator that runs entirely offline on a Raspberry Pi
excerpt: Google and Antigravity built the Gemma Translator, an offline AI translation prototype running Gemma 4 E2B on a Raspberry Pi 5. No internet needed. Open source on GitHub.
content_html:
TL;DR

Google and Antigravity built an offline AI translator prototype on a Raspberry Pi 5 running Gemma 4 E2B. No internet needed. Open source on GitHub. Not a product announcement.

Google and its Antigravity team have built a prototype AI translator that runs entirely offline on a Raspberry Pi 5. The Gemma Translator uses Gemma 4 E2B, the smallest model in Google’s open-weight family, to process speech locally without any cloud connection. The device includes a microphone and speaker inside a custom 3D-printed enclosure, creating a self-contained translation device that works anywhere regardless of connectivity. The project is open source on GitHub.

Google launched Gemma 4 in April with four model sizes, and the E2B edge variant was specifically designed to run on hardware as small as a Raspberry Pi or Jetson Nano. The Translator prototype is the most tangible demonstration of what that means in practice. Most AI translation tools, including Google Translate, require a cloud connection to process speech. Running everything on-device eliminates that dependency, which matters for travellers in areas with poor connectivity, organisations handling sensitive conversations, and emergency responders operating without infrastructure.

This is a technology showcase, not a product announcement. Google has not said it plans to sell the device or integrate it into an existing product. But it points toward a future where AI assistants do not always need data centres to be useful. Antigravity launched as Google’s agentic development platform at I/O, and the Translator is one of the first projects built with it that targets non-developers: a physical device that does one thing well, without an internet connection, on hardware that costs under $100.

As open models continue to shrink while becoming more capable, devices like this could eventually appear in travel gadgets, accessibility tools, classrooms, or disaster response kits. The Raspberry Pi 5 costs about $80. The Gemma 4 E2B model is free under Apache 2.0. The 3D-printed case and the code are open source. The components for a working offline translator are now available to anyone who wants to build one.

content_html_zh:
TL;DR

Google 和 Antigravity 在运行 Gemma 4 E2B 的 Raspberry Pi 5 上构建了离线 AI 翻译器原型。 无需互联网。 在 GitHub 上开源。 不是产品公告。

谷歌及其反重力团队构建了一个人工智能翻译器原型，可以在 Raspberry Pi 5 上完全离线运行。 Gemma Translator 使用 Gemma 4 E2B（Google 开放权重系列中最小的模型）在本地处理语音，无需任何云连接。 该设备在定制的 3D 打印外壳内包含麦克风和扬声器，创建了一个独立的翻译设备，无论连接如何，都可以在任何地方工作。 该项目在 GitHub 上开源。

谷歌于 4 月份推出了 Gemma 4，有四种型号尺寸，E2B 边缘版本专门设计用于在 Raspberry Pi 或 Jetson Nano 等小型硬件上运行。 Translator 原型是这在实践中意味着什么的最具体的演示。 大多数人工智能翻译工具，包括谷歌翻译，都需要云连接来处理语音。 在设备上运行所有内容消除了这种依赖性，这对于网络连接较差地区的旅行者、处理敏感对话的组织以及在没有基础设施的情况下工作的应急响应人员来说很重要。

这是技术展示，而不是产品公告。 谷歌尚未表示计划出售该设备或将其集成到现有产品中。 但这预示着未来人工智能助手并不总是需要数据中心才能发挥作用。 Antigravity 作为 Google 在 I/O 上的代理开发平台推出，而 Translator 是用它构建的首批针对非开发人员的项目之一：一种物理设备，无需互联网连接，在成本低于 100 美元的硬件上就能很好地完成某件事。

随着开放模型不断缩小并变得更加强大，此类设备最终可能会出现在旅行小工具、辅助工具、教室或灾难响应工具包中。 Raspberry Pi 5 的售价约为 80 美元。 Gemma 4 E2B 模型在 Apache 2.0 下是免费的。 3D 打印的案例和代码都是开源的。 现在，任何想要构建离线翻译器的人都可以使用离线翻译器的组件。
